A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LDAR research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison, including matching material across appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original multi-model LaRA experiments, zero-shot HotpotQA/NQ evaluations, and retrieval-strategy analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds efficiency measurements, baseline comparisons, ablations, transfer experiments and Ada-LEval evaluation.

M1.justification: The core architecture, band-selection procedure and policy-gradient update are retained. Appendices D.5 and D.9 add evaluated variants with token-cost regularization, standard learnable embeddings and a pooled MLP encoder. These extend the studied procedures without replacing the main LDAR method.

E1.justification: v2 adds Ada-LEval's BestAnswer task, requiring selection of the most helpful answer among StackOverflow candidates (D.7, Table 8). The existing LaRA tasks and HELMET HotpotQA/NQ coverage are retained.

E2.justification: v2 adds RankZephyr to the main LaRA comparisons and all nine per-model tables, and adds cache-augmented generation, CAG, to efficiency comparisons. These substantively broaden evaluated alternatives to include listwise reranking and document-cache reuse while retaining the previous comparator suite.

E3.justification: New protocols measure end-to-end latency and cumulative training/inference costs at 10K, 100K and 500K inference calls. Additional designs include embedding-model swaps, misaligned task transfers, clustering 100 similarity distributions and sliding windows of 20, 50 and 100 passages. The original split and correctness judging remain unchanged; newly disclosed chunking details do not establish changed preprocessing.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained band-versus-Bernoulli and hallucination-training analyses, v2 adds cost-objective and architecture ablations, cross-embedder generalization and task-alignment tests. New case studies, clustering and sliding-window experiments investigate when broader or non-top-ranked retrieval helps (D.2–D.10).

E5.justification: Figure 11 newly specifies standard-deviation bands across examples for similarity distributions. Existing standard-error reporting across LLMs is retained. Neither version provides explicit seed or repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: Original LDAR accuracy results are retained, while v2 adds substantial baseline, efficiency, ablation and transfer results. New Table 3 reports open-source LDAR/LC latency of 3.9/15.4 seconds, and Table 8 adds BestAnswer results. A retained entry also changes: GPT-4o Top-5's 128K overall token ratio goes from 0.082 to 0.025 (v1 Table 10; v2 Table 16).

T1.justification: Section 4's equations and Algorithm 1 retain the same mathematical content. The added mechanism and transfer discussions are empirical; no new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions and conclusion retain the central claim that capacity-adaptive band retrieval balances coverage and distraction, improving accuracy with fewer tokens. Added experiments support this existing contribution without redefining it.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations involving similarity-scale/rank alignment, task-structure alignment, mid-ranked informative passages and cost-penalty-induced collapse. It also interprets deployment volume as determining training-cost amortization. These substantially expand applicability conditions and mechanism explanations; the original limitations paragraph is merely relocated to Appendix B.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents 600-token chunks with 100-token overlap, RankZephyr's top-50-to-top-5 procedure, and per-document caching for CAG. The anonymous code-access link is replaced by the named GitHub repository. Core LDAR hyperparameters and hardware disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and discussion for CAG, RankZephyr, Ada-LEval, C-pack and Deep Sets. These support added comparisons and analyses; the main related-work organization and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most original prose and the main narrative are preserved. Local revisions clarify baseline descriptions and task alignment, move limitations into Appendix B, reorganize the appendices, and update author, affiliation and publication information. Added scientific sections do not constitute extensive rewriting of the existing text.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands visual presentation with efficiency plots, an annotated case study, rank-agreement and clustering figures, sliding-window plots and ablation tables. Existing comparison tables gain RankZephyr rows. v1 Figures 5–6 are retained as v2 Figures 6–7, while new Table 3 is redisplayed as Table 6.

improvement.justification: v1 supported efficiency mainly through token ratios and offered limited controlled evidence for architectural and transfer assumptions. v2 adds measured latency, training-cost analyses and targeted ablations that substantially strengthen those arguments and expose transfer boundaries. Localized reporting errors temper the gains—for example, Table 15 reports RankZephyr's 128K overall score as 73.3 although its component scores average 48.35—but do not outweigh the stronger empirical validation.
